news.title: AI与ML：关键差异、应用场景及Domo如何释放其全部潜力
news.snippet: 人工智能是指构建能够模拟人类智能系统的广泛领域，机器学习则是其重要分支，二者应用场景各异。
news.raw_snippet:
Artificial intelligence refers to the broad field of building machines that can simulate human decision-making and cognitive functions. It involves using computers and algorithms to analyze data, identify patterns, and solve problems in ways that resemble human intelligence.

Examples of AI include:

 A computer playing chess against a human
 A self-driving car navigating city traffic
 A virtual assistant like Siri or Alexa that can answer questions and perform tasks [...] When you hear about artificial intelligence (AI), you often come across another common term: machine learning (ML). These two are closely related, but they aren’t the same thing. AI is the broader concept of creating machines that can mimic human intelligence. ML is a subset of AI that focuses on teaching computers to learn from data and improve over time without being explicitly programmed. [...] At its core, AI is about enabling machines to reason, plan, and make decisions.

### What is machine learning?

Machine learning is a specific branch of AI focused on using algorithms to analyze data, find patterns, and improve over time. Instead of following fixed instructions, ML models are trained on data to predict outcomes and make decisions.

For example, ML can be trained on thousands of emails to learn how to identify spam, or on years of stock data to forecast financial trends.

news.title: 特朗普科技盟友在财报电话会议中用“超级智能”替代AI
news.snippet: 特朗普科技盟友在财报电话会议中用“超级智能”替代AI，亚马逊CEO安迪·贾西周四频繁提及AI。
news.raw_snippet: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy peppered his call with use of AI on Thursday, uttering the acronym well over a dozen times in his introductory remarks. A day earlier, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said one of the company's three points of focus is "designing AI to empower people." And Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai was seconds into his quarterly earnings commentary when he said the search giant's "AI investments are driving increased usage and overall user growth." [...] That's not to suggest tech execs sticking with "AI" on this week's earnings calls are openly defying the president. Trump's preferred term is seeping into other correspondence and documents. Microsoft's annual report filed last week included eight mentions of super intelligence, starting at the top of the letter to shareholders. [...] IBM CEO Arvind Krishna, who didn't attend Trump's September lunch, used SI alongside AI during his company's earnings call last week. Krishna said, "technology innovation in both hybrid infrastructure and super intelligence is leading to better business performance," adding that IBM is advancing as a "software-led hybrid cloud and AI platform company."
